title: Overrated
style: Alternative R&B, husky smoky female mezzo with powerful full-voice belts; post-punk instrumental production, wiry bass guitar, angular clean electric guitar, taut live-sounding drums and spare keys; tape saturation and soft clipping; mid-tempo pulse.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My mother cheated; that's the tale I knew.
They split my weeks in halves, and so I grew
between my dad's in Worcester and the town
of Lincoln, Rhode Island, where Mom moved down.

At eighteen, Clark was how I got away
from Mom and stepdad's house; I chose to stay
with Dad, whose girlfriend, kind, was fine with me:
a quiet house, a place to simply be.

[Chorus]
Love is overrated. (love is overrated)
The pain is in pretending that it's not.
Love is a scam, (love is a scam)
a guilt trip society has taught.

[Verse 2]
I never missed the sweetheart that I left
in Lincoln, and I did not feel bereft
when Worcester High's romance came to an end.
At college I endured them, two or three,
and nothing stuck; it wasn't meant to be.

[Chorus]
Love is overrated. (love is overrated)
The pain is in pretending that it's not.
Love is a scam, (love is a scam)
a guilt trip society has taught.

[Bridge]
Grown up, I understood my mom.
I love my dad; he's not to blame.
The fault was in the world that sold
a dream of love to young and old.
If they had seen it, they might still
be one, or part without ill will.

[Final Chorus]
Love is overrated.
It sells you chimeras that aren't there.
Love is a scam,
the pain is in pretending that it's not.
It makes you think you're a failure
when you're just a human being.
